Then Marcus started sitting in it voluntarily. He was always early, so he had his pick of the room. Still, every meeting, punishment chair. If someone said, You can take this better one, he'd say he was fine. The strange part was that sometimes he would sit down, roll backward once, stand up, and switch to another bad chair. My teammate became convinced he was avoiding sitting beside our manager. Someone else thought he had back problems and was too polite to say so. Then he started arriving early to conference rooms on other floors and doing the same thing. Sit. Roll. Lean. Switch. It looked like the world's saddest game of musical chairs. One afternoon I asked him directly whether he was testing office furniture. He froze. That reaction told me yes. A week earlier, a colleague from another team had fallen when a chair wheel suddenly detached. She wasn't badly hurt, but facilities couldn't identify which chair had failed because someone had pushed it back into a row before reporting the problem. All the chairs were the same model, and the broken wheel only came loose when weight shifted in a certain direction. Marcus had witnessed the fall. Facilities asked him to help identify the chair while they arranged a full inspection, but they didn't want people panicking or moving chairs between rooms. So Marcus had been quietly checking the suspect chairs before meetings: sitting, rolling a few centimeters, leaning carefully, then marking the underside of anything suspicious with removable tape. He wasn't choosing the worst seat. He was trying to find the genuinely dangerous one before somebody else sat down. Facilities eventually found it in a training room where someone had moved it after the accident. They removed the whole batch for inspection. Marcus became a minor office hero for about two days, which he hated. We stopped calling it the punishment chair. Now whenever he sits down and rolls backward, everyone watches him like he's performing a safety demonstration. I thought he was avoiding people. He was volunteering to lose a fight with office furniture first.
story.twist: He has been testing every chair after facilities asked him to identify the one with an intermittent broken wheel that caused a colleague's fall.
